ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, rectangle $ABCD$ is folded along the diagonal $BD$, with point $C$ falling on point $E$. $BE$ intersects $AD$ at point $F$. Given that $\angle BDC=62^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle DFE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that quadrilateral ABCD is a rectangle, \\
$\therefore$ $AD\parallel BC$ and $\angle ADC=90^\circ$, \\
Given $\angle BDC=62^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle FDB=90^\circ-\angle BDC=90^\circ-62^\circ=28^\circ$, \\
Since $AD\parallel BC$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle CBD=\angle FDB=28^\circ$, \\
Since rectangle ABCD is folded along the diagonal BD, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle FBD=\angle CBD=28^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle DFE=\angle FBD+\angle FDB=28^\circ+28^\circ=\boxed{56^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached diagram, ABCD is drawn as a rectangle with A at the upper left, B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and D at the upper right. Segment BD is drawn as a diagonal. Point E is above the top side AD, and segment BE crosses AD at F. The angle at D between DB and DC is marked 62°. Reasoning: Since ABCD is a rectangle, AD is perpendicular to DC, so ∠ADC = 90°. Because F lies on AD, ray DF is along AD. The given angle ∠BDC is the angle between DB and DC, equal to 62°, so the angle between DB and AD at D is ∠FDB = 90° − 62° = 28°. Also, in a rectangle AD ∥ BC, so the angle that DB makes with BC at B equals the angle that DB makes with AD at D; hence ∠CBD = ∠FDB = 28°. Folding along diagonal BD reflects point C to E and ray BC to ray BE. Since F lies on BE, ∠FBD = ∠CBD = 28°. In triangle BDF, FE is an extension of FB, so ∠DFE is the exterior angle at F. Therefore ∠DFE = ∠FBD + ∠FDB = 28° + 28° = 56°.
